examples.en: After work, I went to the hospital to visit my sick friend.

examples.ko: 회사 동료가 입원해서 다 같이 문병했어요.
examples.en: A coworker was hospitalized, so we all visited him together.
How about we visit him in the hospital together tomorrow?

examples.ko: 병원에서 문병할 때는 조용히 해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to be quiet when you visit someone in the hospital.
I visited my grandmother in the hospital and gave her some fruit.
I went to visit my teacher in the hospital last week.

explain: 아픈 사람을 병원이나 집으로 찾아가 보는 일이라 목적어가 사람이에요. '선생님을 문병하다'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '병문안(을) 가다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for going to see a sick person, so the object is a person, as in '선생님을 문병하다'. In daily talk people also often say '병문안(을) 가다'.

examples.en: I saved the files I received in the document folder.
I'll look for the contract in the document folder.

examples.ko: 문서함이 가득 차서 오래된 파일을 지웠어요.
examples.en: The document folder was full, so I deleted old files.
This document folder only has last month's reports.
I organized the document folder, and now it's much easier to find things.

examples.ko: 중요한 문서는 따로 문서함으로 옮겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please move important documents to the document folder separately.

explain: '메일함', '쪽지함'처럼 '-함'이 붙은 이름이에요. 회사 시스템이나 앱 화면에서 자주 보여요. 종이 서류를 넣어 두는 상자는 보통 '서류함'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Like '메일함' (mailbox) and '쪽지함' (message box), it is a name ending in '-함'. You often see it in company systems and app screens. A box for paper documents is usually called '서류함'.

examples.en: I boiled octopus legs and ate them at the market.
These octopus legs are soft, not tough.
That company expanded its business like an octopus spreading its legs.
I bought an octopus leg skewer on the street.
It's dangerous to plug many things into one outlet like that.
My child likes octopus-shaped sausages.

explain: 음식 재료로는 '문어 다리'와 같은 말이에요. 뉴스나 회화에서는 여러 갈래로 뻗는 모습을 비유할 때 많이 써요. 콘센트 하나에 여러 플러그를 꽂는 것도 '문어발'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That company expanded its business in every direction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 회사가 관련 없는 분야까지 여기저기 사업을 늘릴 때 써요. 대체로 부정적인 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a company spreads into many unrelated fields. It usually sounds negative.
phrases.en_equiv: sprawling expansion; spreading oneself too thin

explain_en: As food it means the same as '문어 다리' (octopus legs). In news and conversation it is often used figuratively for something spreading in many directions. Plugging many plugs into one outlet is also called '문어발'.

en: treat as a problem; make an issue of

examples.en: The boss did not treat the small mistake as a problem.
The school treats frequent lateness as a serious problem.

examples.ko: 그 일을 문제시하는 사람이 아무도 없어요.
examples.en: No one sees that matter as a problem.

examples.ko: 이 점을 문제시했으면 더 빨리 고쳤을 거예요.
examples.en: If they had treated this as a problem, they would have fixed it sooner.
I was surprised that my team leader made an issue of my way of speaking.

examples.ko: 그 정도는 굳이 문제시할 필요가 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to make an issue of something like that.

explain: '문제 삼다'와 비슷한 말인데 더 딱딱해서 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 '문제 삼다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요. '문제시되다'처럼 피동 형태로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '문제 삼다' (to make an issue of) but sounds stiffer and appears more in writing and news. In speech, '문제 삼다' often feels more natural. The passive form '문제시되다' is also common.

examples.en: The gatekeeper blocked the way in front of the castle gate.
I told the gatekeeper my name and went in.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기에는 무서운 문지기를 만나는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: Old stories have scenes where you meet a scary gatekeeper.

examples.ko: 동화 속 문지기는 열쇠를 숨기고 있었어요.
examples.en: The gatekeeper in the fairy tale was hiding the key.

examples.ko: 문지기의 허락 없이는 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't enter without the gatekeeper's permission.
I stood guard in front of the entrance all night like a gatekeeper.

explain: 요즘 건물에서는 '경비원'이라고 하고, '문지기'는 옛이야기나 성, 대문 같은 장면에서 더 자주 나와요. 누군가가 들어오는 것을 막거나 허락하는 사람을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: For modern buildings people say '경비원' (security guard), while '문지기' appears more in old tales, castles and gates. It can also describe someone who controls who gets in.

examples.en: I'm tall, so I hit my head on the doorframe.

examples.ko: 문틀이 휘어서 문이 잘 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: The doorframe is warped, so the door doesn't close well.
I called a company to install a new doorframe.
I wiped the dust off the doorframe with a rag.

examples.ko: 문틀 위에 작은 화분을 올려 두었어요.
examples.en: I put a small flowerpot on top of the doorframe.

examples.ko: 이 문틀은 나무가 아니라 철로 만들었어요.
examples.en: This doorframe is made of metal, not wood.

explain: 문짝을 끼우는 둘레의 틀이에요. 창문 쪽은 '창틀'이라고 하고, 바닥 쪽의 턱은 '문턱'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is the frame around the opening that holds the door. For windows it is '창틀', and the raised bar at the bottom is '문턱', which is a different thing.

examples.en: Cold wind comes in through the gap in the door.
My finger got caught in the door gap and it hurt.
The gap around the door is wide, so bugs come in.
Light leaked out through the crack in the door.
I sealed the door gap with tape, and it's less cold now.
I heard laughter through the crack in the door.

explain: 문과 문틀 사이처럼 좁게 벌어진 곳이에요. '문틈으로 엿보다', '문틈에 끼이다', '문틈으로 바람이 들어오다'처럼 짝지어 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the narrow gap between a door and its frame. It pairs naturally with phrases like '문틈으로 엿보다' (peek through the crack), '문틈에 끼이다' (get caught in the gap) and '문틈으로 바람이 들어오다' (wind comes through).

examples.en: People from the cultural world gathered at the event.
The cultural community was shocked by this incident.
That actor is a respected figure in the cultural field.
I read cultural news in the culture section of the newspaper.
That person has led the cultural field for a long time.
The reaction of the cultural community was mostly positive.

explain: 문화·예술 일을 하는 사람들과 그 분야 전체를 묶어서 말할 때 써요. '정치계', '연예계'처럼 '-계'가 붙은 말이고, 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It refers to the people and the whole field of culture and the arts together. Like '정치계' (political world) and '연예계' (entertainment world), it uses '-계' and often appears in news and articles.

examples.en: If cultures differ, even the meaning of a smile differs.
Korea belongs to the Chinese-character cultural sphere.

examples.ko: 다른 문화권 사람과 일하면 배울 점이 많아요.
examples.en: Working with people from another culture teaches you a lot.
The way people greet each other differs by cultural region.

examples.ko: 이 음식은 여러 문화권에서 비슷하게 먹어요.
examples.en: This food is eaten in a similar way in many cultural regions.

examples.ko: 다른 문화권을 이해하려면 먼저 질문해 보세요.
examples.en: To understand another culture, start by asking questions.

explain: 나라 경계와 달리 언어, 종교, 생활 습관이 비슷한 넓은 지역을 묶어 말해요. '한자 문화권', '이슬람 문화권'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: Unlike a country, it groups together wide areas that share similar language, religion or customs. It takes a word in front, as in '한자 문화권' or '이슬람 문화권'.

examples.en: I tagged along in my friend's car and arrived comfortably.
Is it okay if I tag along too?

examples.ko: 조별 과제에서 혼자 묻어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't just coast on others' work in a group project.

examples.ko: 이번에는 아무도 묻어갈 생각을 하지 마세요.
examples.en: This time, nobody should think about coasting on others.
I don't like riding on other people's efforts.
My younger sibling quietly tagged along to our gathering.

explain: 남이 하는 일이나 모임, 이동 수단에 큰 힘을 들이지 않고 끼어서 함께 가는 거예요. 친구 사이에서는 '나도 묻어가도 돼?'처럼 가볍게 부탁하고, 일에서는 '무임승차'처럼 조금 부정적일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means joining in on someone else's activity, gathering or ride without much effort of your own. Among friends you can ask lightly, '나도 묻어가도 돼?', while about work it can sound a bit negative, like free-riding.

examples.en: I decided to keep that story buried in my heart.

examples.ko: 오래된 비밀을 평생 묻어둘 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't keep an old secret buried for a lifetime.
If you bury potatoes in soil, they last a long time.

examples.ko: 아이는 상처를 혼자 묻어둔 채 지냈어요.
examples.en: The child kept the hurt buried inside and went on living.

examples.ko: 그 문제를 계속 묻어둬서 더 커졌어요.
examples.en: We kept burying that problem, so it got bigger.

examples.ko: 좋은 아이디어를 묻어두지 말고 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't keep your good idea to yourself; say it out loud.

explain: 땅에 묻어서 그대로 두는 것뿐 아니라, 말이나 문제를 꺼내지 않고 그냥 두는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 이때는 '덮어두다'와 비슷하고, 반대로 '꺼내다', '털어놓다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Besides literally burying something and leaving it, it is often used for leaving a word or problem unspoken. In that sense it is close to '덮어두다', and its opposites are '꺼내다' and '털어놓다'.

examples.en: The blue wave pattern on this curtain is pretty.
I bought a dress with a wave pattern.
I drew a wave pattern around the edge of the plate.
The wind left a wave-like pattern in the sand.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 물결무늬라서 소스가 잘 묻어요.
examples.en: This snack has a wavy pattern, so the sauce sticks well.
This cup has a handle decorated with a wave pattern.

explain: '줄무늬', '체크무늬', '물방울무늬'처럼 무늬 이름을 말할 때 써요. 물결처럼 구불구불 이어지는 모양이면 물이 아닌 모래나 천에도 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: Like '줄무늬' (stripes), '체크무늬' (checks) and '물방울무늬' (polka dots), it is a pattern name. Anything that curves in a wavy line can be described this way, even sand or fabric.

examples.en: When the wind blew, the barley field rippled like waves.
The lake is gently rippling.
The flags of the cheering crowd wave like a sea.
I looked at the sea, rolling with waves, for a long time.
Her long hair flowed in the wind, and it looked pretty.
The cheers of the people will surge through the square.

explain: 실제 물뿐 아니라 밀밭, 머리카락, 깃발, 사람들의 감정이 파도처럼 이어서 움직이는 모습에도 써요. 말할 때보다 글이나 묘사에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used for real water but also for wheat fields, hair, flags and people's emotions moving in a wave-like way. You see it more in writing and description than in everyday speech.

examples.en: The child leans on the wall and practices handstands.
You need arm strength to do a handstand.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 물구나무서기를 하고 걸을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling can even walk while doing a handstand.
Handstands were hard, so I kept falling over.
We bet on who could hold a handstand the longest.

examples.ko: 물구나무서기 자세로 십 초만 버텨 보세요.
examples.en: Try holding the handstand position for just ten seconds.

explain: 손으로 바닥을 짚고 거꾸로 서는 동작이에요. 동사로는 '물구나무서다'나 '물구나무를 서다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is the move of standing upside down on your hands. As a verb you can say '물구나무서다' or '물구나무를 서다'.

examples.en: When the whale breathed, a column of water shot up.
The fountain shot a tall column of water into the air.

examples.ko: 소방차 호스에서 물기둥처럼 물이 뿜어져 나왔어요.
examples.en: Water burst out of the fire truck's hose like a pillar.
A rainbow appeared between the columns of water.
The children played happily under the columns of water.
The column of water was as tall as a building.

explain: 굵고 높게 솟아오르는 물줄기를 말해요. 가늘게 흐르는 '물줄기'와 달리 고래, 분수, 부딪히는 파도처럼 힘 있게 솟는 모습에 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes a thick, tall jet of water rising up. Unlike the thin flowing '물줄기', it suits powerful scenes like whales, fountains and crashing waves.

examples.en: This neighborhood suffers flooding every rainy season.
There was flooding because of the rain yesterday.
The underground parking lot was a mess because of the flood.
School was closed because of the flooding.
Luckily, no one was hurt despite the flooding.
Volunteers gathered at the flood site.

explain: 큰비 때문에 생기는 홍수 피해뿐 아니라, 집 안에 수도관이 터져 물바다가 되는 일에도 써요. '물난리가 나다', '물난리를 겪다'처럼 말하고, '수해'보다 편한 말투예요.
explain_en: It covers flood damage from heavy rain, and also a home flooded by a burst pipe. It is said as '물난리가 나다' or '물난리를 겪다', and sounds more casual than '수해'.

examples.en: The peach was very soft, so I ate it right away.
This bread is soft and moist.
When persimmons get soft, they are sweet and tasty.
The rice turned out mushy.
I tend to like soft jelly.
The ground was soaked by rain and soft.

explain: '말랑말랑하다'는 보통 기분 좋은 부드러움이고, '물렁물렁하다'는 단단해야 할 것이 너무 무르다는 느낌으로도 많이 써요. 과일, 밥, 젖은 땅 등에 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '말랑말랑하다' usually sounds pleasantly soft, while '물렁물렁하다' is often used when something that should be firm is too soft. It is common for fruit, rice and wet ground.

examples.en: If you press the cartilage in your ear, it feels soft.

examples.ko: 코는 물렁뼈로 되어 있어서 잘 구부러져요.
examples.en: The nose is made of cartilage, so it bends easily.
I ordered fried chicken cartilage.
My knee cartilage wore down, so I went to the hospital.
Cartilage is softer than hard bone.
The doctor checked the condition of the cartilage.

explain: 병원이나 수업에서는 같은 뜻의 '연골'이라는 말도 많이 써요. '물렁뼈'는 닭 연골 요리 같은 음식 이야기나 일상 대화에서도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: At hospitals and in classes the same thing is also called '연골'. '물렁뼈' also comes up in daily conversation and food talk, such as chicken cartilage dishes.

examples.en: The water mill turns slowly by the stream.
In the old days, people pounded grain with a water mill.
I looked at the water mill at the folk village.
I rested while listening to the sound of the water mill.
This cafe's garden even has a water mill.
The sight of water falling onto the water mill was beautiful.

explain: 요즘은 일상에서 보기 어려워서 민속촌, 관광지, 정원 장식에서 주로 만나요. 옛 시골 풍경을 이야기할 때 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is rarely seen in daily life now, so you mostly meet it at folk villages, tourist spots and garden decorations. It often comes up when describing old countryside scenery.

examples.en: I use liquid soap when I wash my hands.
We've run out of liquid soap in the bathroom.
Liquid soap lathers well, so it's convenient.
I bought a liquid soap refill at the mart.
Can I wash dishes with liquid soap?
One drop of liquid soap is enough.

explain: 딱딱한 '비누'와 달리 액체로 되어 있고 펌프 용기에 담아 쓰는 비누예요. 손 씻는 용도로는 '핸드워시'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike a hard bar of '비누', it is liquid and usually comes in a pump bottle. For hand washing, people also say '핸드워시'.

examples.en: The color of the lake water is clear and blue.
In a light blue dress, you look cool and fresh.
In the sunset, the color of the water turned red.
The child gazed at the color of the water for a long time.
I painted the wall light blue.
There wasn't a single cloud in the light blue sky.

explain: 물의 색이나 연한 푸른색을 말해요. 글이나 시에서 느낌 있게 쓰이고, 일상에서는 '하늘색'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It means the color of water, or a pale blue. It has a poetic feel in writing, and in daily talk people also say '하늘색'.

examples.en: I watered the plants with a watering can.
I left the watering can on the balcony.
The watering can is old and its holes are clogged.

examples.ko: 물뿌리개 대신 페트병으로 물을 줘도 돼요.
examples.en: You can water plants with a plastic bottle instead of a watering can.
Water comes out gently from this watering can.
Please fill the watering can with water.

explain: 꽃이나 화분에 물을 줄 때 쓰는 도구예요. 일상에서는 '물조리개'라고도 말해요. 주로 '물뿌리개로 물을 주다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the tool used to water flowers and pots. In daily talk it is also called '물조리개'. It is mostly used as '물뿌리개로 물을 주다'.

examples.en: Mist rose over the lake in the morning.
I walked slowly along the misty riverside.
The mountain wrapped in mist looked mysterious.
The water mist soon disappears when the sun rises.
Photographers come at dawn to photograph the mist.
I remember his face faintly, like mist.

explain: 강이나 호수, 바다 위에 피어오르는 안개를 말해요. 그냥 '안개'보다 물가의 새벽 풍경이 떠오르는 말이고, 글이나 여행 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means fog rising over a river, lake or sea. Compared with plain '안개', it brings to mind a dawn scene by the water and often appears in writing and travel stories.

examples.en: I got a mosquito bite, so I put liquid pain reliever on it.
It stings if the liquid pain reliever gets in your eyes.
Liquid pain reliever feels cool when you apply it.
I bought a bottle of liquid pain reliever at the pharmacy.
There is also liquid pain reliever in Mom's drawer.
I rubbed the insect bite with liquid pain reliever.

explain: 붙이는 '파스'와 달리 액체를 발라서 쓰는 약이에요. 어깨가 뻐근할 때나 벌레 물린 곳에 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: Unlike the adhesive '파스' patch, this is a liquid you rub on. People often use it for stiff shoulders or insect bites.

examples.en: I wiped my hands with a wet tissue at the restaurant.
I keep a pack of wet tissues in my bag.
The wet tissues dried out, so I can't use them.
There are separate wet tissues for babies.
Could you give me just one wet tissue?
I also put wet tissues in the car.

explain: 물에 적셔 나오는 티슈로, 손이나 테이블을 닦을 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '물티슈'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a pre-moistened tissue used for wiping hands or tables. In everyday talk people also commonly say '물티슈'.

examples.ko: 죽이 너무 묽어서 쌀을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: The porridge was too thin, so I added more rice.

examples.ko: 묽은 수프는 빵에 찍어 먹기 어려워요.
examples.en: Thin soup is hard to eat by dipping bread in it.

examples.ko: 물감이 너무 묽으면 가루를 조금 더 섞으세요.
examples.en: If the paint is too thin, mix in a little more powder.

examples.ko: 반죽이 묽지 않게 밀가루를 조금 더 넣어요.
examples.en: Add a bit more flour so the batter isn't runny.
This yogurt is thinner than I expected.
The paint went on thin, so the color is pale.

explain: 국물, 죽, 반죽, 물감처럼 농도가 진하지 않고 물기가 많을 때 써요. '싱겁다'는 맛이 약한 거고 '묽다'는 걸쭉한 정도라서 달라요. 반대말은 '되다'나 '진하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes soup, porridge, batter or paint that is not thick and has a lot of liquid. '싱겁다' is about weak flavor, while '묽다' is about thickness, so they differ. Its opposites are '되다' and '진하다'.

examples.en: White fluffy clouds are floating in the sky.
Fluffy clouds remind me of cotton candy.
The shape of puffy clouds keeps changing.
Sunlight shone through the puffy clouds.
It's a cake as fluffy as a cloud.
I want to lie down on the fluffy clouds.

explain: 몽실몽실하게 위로 솟은 하얀 구름이에요. 맑은 날 여름 하늘에서 많이 보여서 그림이나 동요, 시에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: These are white clouds that billow upward in rounded puffs. They are often seen in clear summer skies and appear in drawings, children's songs and poems.

examples.en: Children are playing on the slide at the playground.
I laid an anti-slip mat in the bathroom.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 길이 얼어서 미끄럼 사고가 나요.
examples.en: In winter the roads freeze, and slipping accidents happen.
Watch out for slipping on snowy days.
My younger sibling likes going down the slide the most.
Walk slowly on very slippery ice.

explain: 주로 '미끄럼(을) 타다', '미끄럼틀', '미끄럼 방지'처럼 합쳐서 써요. 넘어질 듯 미끄러지는 동작은 '미끄러지다', 표면 상태는 '미끄럽다'를 써요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in combinations like '미끄럼(을) 타다' (go down a slide), '미끄럼틀' (slide) and '미끄럼 방지' (anti-slip). For the action of slipping use '미끄러지다', and for a slippery surface use '미끄럽다'.

examples.en: How do you make the future form in Korean?
Try changing this sentence into the future form.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 건물이 모두 미래형이라서 신기해요.
examples.en: All the buildings in this city look futuristic, which is amazing.
I went to a futuristic car exhibition.

examples.ko: 내일 일정을 말할 때 미래형을 써요.
examples.en: I use the future form when talking about tomorrow's plans.
This building really looks futuristic.

explain: 문법에서는 '-(으)ㄹ 거예요' 같은 미래를 나타내는 형태를 가리켜요. 한국어는 '내일 가요'처럼 현재형으로도 미래를 말해요. '미래형 도시'처럼 명사 앞에 붙으면 미래적인 모습을 가리켜요.
explain_en: In grammar, it refers to forms that express the future, such as '-(으)ㄹ 거예요'. Korean can also talk about the future with the present form, as in '내일 가요'. Before a noun, as in '미래형 도시', it refers to a futuristic look.

examples.en: The baby was born prematurely and is in the hospital.
Premature babies need special care.
My friend's baby was born premature but grew up well.
The nurse took careful care of the premature baby.
I heard there is a support program for premature babies.
My nephew was premature too, so we were worried at first.

explain: 예정보다 일찍 태어난 아기를 말해요. 병원이나 뉴스에서는 '조산아'라는 말도 같이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 조심스러운 주제라 말투를 부드럽게 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a baby born earlier than expected. In hospitals and news, '조산아' is also used. It is a sensitive topic, so people keep their tone gentle in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 미숫가루를 물에 타 마셔요.
examples.en: On hot days I mix misugaru with water and drink it.
I added milk to the misugaru, and it tastes nutty.
This is misugaru my grandmother made herself.

examples.ko: 미숫가루는 한 끼 대신 먹기도 해요.
examples.en: Some people have misugaru instead of a meal.
Would you like a glass of misugaru?
Misugaru clumps, so you have to stir it well.

explain: 곡식을 가루로 만든 것을 찬물이나 우유에 타서 마시는 음식이에요. '미싯가루'라고 잘못 쓰는 일이 많은데, 표준 표기는 '미숫가루'예요.
explain_en: It is a powder of ground grains that you mix into cold water or milk to drink. Many people misspell it as '미싯가루', but the standard spelling is '미숫가루'.

examples.en: It's a superstitious story, so I don't believe it.

examples.ko: 그분은 꽤 미신적이라서 날짜를 꼭 따져요.
examples.en: He is quite superstitious, so he always checks the date.

examples.ko: 시험 날 미역국을 안 먹는 건 좀 미신적이에요.
examples.en: Not eating seaweed soup on exam day is a bit superstitious.
It may sound superstitious, but I have a jinx.
Don't rely only on superstitious beliefs.

examples.ko: 그 영화에는 미신적 요소가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: That movie has many superstitious elements.

explain: '과학적'의 반대 느낌으로, 근거 없는 믿음에 기대는 태도를 말해요. 약간 부정적인 평가가 담겨 있어서 사람에게 직접 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요. '미신적인 생각'처럼 '인'을 붙이거나 '미신적 믿음'처럼 바로 써요.
explain_en: Its feel is the opposite of '과학적' (scientific): relying on beliefs with no basis. It carries a slightly negative judgment, so saying it directly to a person can be rude. Use it as '미신적인 생각' or directly as '미신적 믿음'.

examples.en: I felt a bit sorry toward my friends for coming late.
I feel a bit bad asking for a favor again.
He held out a gift with a sheepish, apologetic face.
I feel awkward about always being the one treated.
I felt so awkwardly sorry that I couldn't even greet properly.
He smiled sheepishly and bowed his head.

explain: '미안하다'보다 가볍고 쑥스러운 느낌으로, 큰 잘못이 아닌 일에 마음이 불편할 때 써요. 실제로 사과할 때는 '미안해요'가 자연스럽고, '미안쩍다'는 내 마음을 설명할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It feels lighter and more bashful than '미안하다', used when you feel awkward about something that isn't a big mistake. When actually apologizing, '미안해요' is natural; '미안쩍다' is more for describing your own feeling.

en: be packed with; be full of

examples.en: The subway is jam-packed during rush hour.
The amusement park was bursting with people on the weekend.
I packed the bag so full it could burst.
The store is packed on the first day of the sale.
The bus was so packed that I let one go.

examples.ko: 미어터지는 식당 앞에서 한 시간을 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited an hour in front of the jam-packed restaurant.

explain: 사람이나 물건이 너무 많아서 터질 것 같을 때 쓰는 구어체 표현이에요. '붐비다'보다 훨씬 강하고 생생한 느낌이라 친구와 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a colloquial word for when there are so many people or things that it feels ready to burst. It is much stronger and more vivid than '붐비다', so it fits chats with friends.

examples.en: My child had a slight fever, so he stayed home from school.
I have a mild fever, but I'm not badly sick.
My body feels sluggish because of a slight fever.
When I took my temperature, it was only a slight fever.
A mild fever and a cough have continued for days.
In the evening I feel weak from a mild fever.

explain: 몸이 조금 뜨거운 정도의 약한 열이에요. 반대로 높은 열은 '고열'이라고 해요. 병원에서는 '미열이 있다', '미열이 나다'처럼 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a low-grade fever where the body is only a little warm. A high fever is '고열'. At the doctor's it is said as '미열이 있다' or '미열이 나다'.

examples.en: The bath water was lukewarm, so I heated it more.
The coffee cooled down and is lukewarm.
I drank a glass of lukewarm barley tea.
Don't answer that question in a half-hearted way.
It tastes bad if it's lukewarm, so I'll microwave it.
It rained, and even the air felt lukewarm.

explain: 뜨겁지도 차갑지도 않아서 어중간한 온도에 써요. 비슷한 말 '미지근하다'도 있고, 둘 다 온도뿐 아니라 시원하지 않은 반응이나 태도에도 말해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 기대만큼 뜨겁지 않고 별로 관심이 없는 반응을 말할 때 써요. 온도와 상관없이 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a reaction that isn't as enthusiastic as hoped. It is a figurative use unrelated to temperature.

explain_en: It is used for a temperature that is neither hot nor cold. A similar word is '미지근하다', and both can describe not only temperature but also a half-hearted reaction or attitude.

examples.en: Admission is free for children under school age.
Our second child isn't in school yet.

examples.ko: 미취학 시기에는 놀이로 배우는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: In the pre-school years, learning through play is important.

examples.ko: 이 놀이방은 미취학 어린이만 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only pre-school children can enter this play room.

examples.ko: 미취학 자녀가 있는 가족은 먼저 들어오세요.
examples.en: Families with pre-school children, please come in first.
I picked out picture books for pre-school children.

explain: 초등학교에 들어가기 전인 아이를 가리킬 때 써요. 대부분 '미취학 아동', '미취학 자녀'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙어요. 반대로 학교에 다니는 것은 '취학'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a child who hasn't started elementary school yet. It mostly takes a noun after it, as in '미취학 아동' or '미취학 자녀'. Entering school is called '취학'.

examples.en: Check whether the taxi meter is on.
The fare was already showing on the meter.
Driver, please turn on the meter.

examples.ko: 미터기 요금과 카드 결제 금액이 같아요.
examples.en: The meter fare and the card payment amount are the same.
The meter starts from the base fare.

examples.ko: 가스 미터기 숫자를 사진으로 찍어 보냈어요.
examples.en: I took a photo of the numbers on the gas meter and sent it.

explain: 주로 택시에서 거리와 시간에 따라 요금을 보여 주는 기계를 말해요. 전기나 가스처럼 사용량을 재는 기계는 '계량기'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It mainly means the machine in a taxi that shows the fare by distance and time. A device that measures usage, like electricity or gas, is also called '계량기'.
